access.accountWall: Straight after the last question of every quiz (step *_step_user, "Almost done! Your details": first name, last name, date of birth, email, password, GP and consent ticks). It comes BEFORE any result: the plan choice and the consultation screen are only shown after /quiz/step/register.
blockers: Account wall before results: the recommendation screen and the consultation screen could not be seen live.
Some SKUs in the rules (PHI1220, PHI1221, PHI1306, PHI1307, PHI1309, PHI1749, women's add-ons, scalp products) have no public product page that could be found, so their names are unknown.
access.coverageNote: Both hair-loss quizzes were walked live to the account wall with the protocol baselines (runs r05, r07); every screen matched the served quiz definition. The full quiz definition (all questions, show-if conditions, product rules with conditions and blockers, and the no-results template) is served in every quiz page and was saved; product effects for every option were computed by running the site's own rule logic (ported to scratch/engine.py) one change at a time from each baseline. These are "code" findings: the results page itself is after the wall. The scalp quiz was walked live to the wall with a synthetic baseline (r08). One wall check (exp-01) confirmed that a man whose answers block every product meets the same wall with no warning.

engineSummary: All logic is client-side and visible. Each product SKU has a rule: "conditions" (pattern, density, age, scalp state) that must be true and "blockers" (safety answers) that must all be false; questions are matched by their label text. Every SKU that passes is listed, split into "Recommended" and "Other" groups. If nothing passes, the person is sent to a paid trichologist consultation (virtual from £200, clinic from £345). Results of either kind are shown only after an account is created. The three routes are therefore: subscribe (some SKU passes), consultation (all blocked), and the clinic booking link that skips the quiz.
strengths: Whole quiz in plain sight and logically simple: a clear triage to subscription or consultation.
Distinct consultation fallback with a calendar (trichologist or senior trichologist, male or female consultant) instead of a flat refusal.
Women have their own quiz with scalp-symptom triage and a shedding route (cosmetic drops).
Scalp-first philosophy: scalp symptoms swap hair-loss plans for scalp plans or a consultation; a separate scalp quiz exists.
Leaflets state plainly that the products are unlicensed and compounded under pharmacist supervision; the men's start screen makes the person confirm it.
weaknesses: Account wall before any result: the person gives name, DOB, email and password before learning whether they get a plan or a £200+ consultation.

Configuration errors in served rules: blood-pressure blocker has a leading space (minoxidil still offered with uncontrolled BP); the 3% Combination Plan rule can never fire; PHI1230 and PHI1770-1772 can never fire; label typos ("curerrently", "redness??").

Women: sudden onset with a widening parting is not routed to a consultation; post-menopausal women are never offered the finasteride drops despite the leaflet saying they suit them; menopause and HRT answers are unused.
Mixed messages: the men's treatments page says "FULLY LICENSED - Tested and certified for the UK" while the leaflets and start screen say unlicensed.

Different prices for the same product on two store views (oral finasteride £40 vs £42); virtual consultation "from £150" on one page and "from £200" on the price list; dosing 2 ml vs 2.5 ml on different pages.
No exact age question (bands only, no under-18 option); no blood pressure or heart questions beyond one tick-box; medicines are free text no rule reads.
Who prescribes is not stated anywhere seen (trichologists are not prescribers; the leaflet only says "pharmacist supervision").
opportunities: Show the outcome (plan or consultation) before asking for an account, or at least say which route the person is on.
A prescriber-led women's offer: PK's women's online route is minoxidil-type drops or cosmetic shedding drops only; no spironolactone, no finasteride for post-menopausal women online.
Clear, consistent licensing and prescriber information as a trust advantage.
A cheaper, faster path for people PK routes to a £200-£345 consultation (sudden shedding, mild scalp symptoms) with a photo review by a prescriber.

limitations: The results page is behind the account wall, so the real plan list, its order, the default choice and plan-length prices (1/2/3-month) were not seen; product effects come from running the served rules, not from a live results screen.

The server may hide retired SKUs (for example PHI1220/PHI1221) on the results page; if so, Patchy/Extensive men and men with psoriasis/redness/acne would reach the consultation screen instead. This cannot be tested without an account.

Product prices are the single prices shown on product pages; whether they are per month or per 3-month delivery is not stated clearly (the pages say the plan "rolls on a three monthly basis"; the treatments page says every 1, 2 or 3 months).
Several SKUs could not be named. Contents of the 3%/5% and Healthy Scalp combination plans are partly inferred from their names.
Who prescribes and which pharmacy compounds and dispenses was not found in public pages.
